clue.text: This may put a different complexion on what stag at bay has to do

definitions.text: This may put a different complexion on
definitions.meaning: a beauty treatment spread over the skin to improve its look

definitions.text: what stag at bay has to do
definitions.meaning: a cornered deer must turn and confront the hounds chasing it

explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic mask changes the skin's look, and a hunted deer at bay must confront the hounds.

clue.text: Pretty brief enticement brings downfall

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, dropping its last letter

parts.note: fair means pretty
a lure is an enticement

explanation.surface: A short-lived pretty temptation leads to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin or collapse, a lack of success.

clue.text: One doesn't volunteer to do what actor must

definitions.meaning: someone called up for compulsory military service
an actor must con (learn) the script

explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is enlisted compulsorily; read as two words it is learning the lines.

clue.text: Arriving too early, interpreter mistranslates a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the words is taken

explanation.surface: An interpreter arriving early gets some of the translation wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes the run from inside 'interpreter mistranslates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a baby born before full gestation, i.e. premature.

clue.text: Producing much evidence of debts after arrest

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the previous one

parts.note: to cop is to arrest or catch
IOUs are written promises showing money owed

explanation.surface: After an arrest, a lot of evidence about debts turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant, plentiful, yielding a great quantity.

clue.text: A fair chance of prize ring success

definitions.text: A fair chance of prize ring success

parts.words: A fair chance of prize ring success
parts.note: reads like a boxer's prospects in the prize ring, but describes a fairground game where you win by landing a ring over a prize

explanation.definitionFit: A fairground stall game in which hoops are thrown over prizes to win them.

clue.text: Going off playing area, decision hopefully just reached here

parts.note: meat that is going off is high
a court is a playing area, as for tennis

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the pitch, hoping the decision is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is in the sense of fair: courts should reach just verdicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior law court where judgements are delivered, ideally justly.

clue.text: Perhaps bum is on seat here for travel?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A person's backside is on a seat while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a bus, where a passenger sits while travelling.

clue.text: Apprentice King-Emperor wanting nothing

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A trainee king-emperor lacks everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee or novice still being taught.

clue.text: Post name in appropriate position to get local work

indicators.note: to post something is to put it in place, so the name is put into the phrase

parts.note: in keeping means fitting or appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a name in the right place to get a job locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' tells you to place N inside IN KEEPING. A 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, so local work is running one.
explanation.definitionFit: Running an inn or pub, which the British call the local, is the trade meant.

clue.text: Cattle not watered

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or bovine animals
a drink served straight, without water added

explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are an archaic sense, and spirits served undiluted are described this way.

clue.text: Cobbleigh's taking taxi to pub shortly — not a free house

parts.note: Uncle Tom Cobbleigh is the last name in the folk song Widecombe Fair
a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A man takes a taxi to a pub that is tied to a brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'free house' is a pub not tied to one brewery; here the phrase means a home that was not free, the slave's cabin of Stowe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel names the dwelling of an enslaved man, a house of unfreedom.

clue.text: Appearing stupid in games and puzzles

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled and set down foolishly

explanation.surface: Someone looks foolish while playing games and doing puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles and mysteries are puzzles that baffle.

clue.text: Content always found up in a part of roof

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a gable is the triangular end part of a roof

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: e'er is a poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: Something always satisfied is found up in the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like a noun or verb but is the adjective meaning willing; 'always' is the poetic e'er, which 'up' sends upwards in this down clue before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Content in the sense of willing or happy to go along.

clue.text: Brief guide on screen unknown

parts.note: a cursor is the pointer guiding you on a computer screen
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A short guide on screen leaves something unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty, superficial glance is short and quick.

clue.text: Working at idea to capture honours?

definitions.text: Working at idea to capture honours?

parts.note: on means working, functioning

indicators.note: to capture means one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a theme is a central idea
in card games the ace and king are honours, A and K

explanation.surface: Someone works at an idea in the hope of winning awards.
explanation.walkthrough: Honours in bridge are the top cards: ace (A) and king (K).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone ambitiously seeking gain or advancement.

clue.text: Rook entering pecked another bird

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pecked means bitten
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook attacks and pecks another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the bird, but it is the chess piece R.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron-like marsh bird, the second bird after the rook.

clue.text: Very short distance wrongly seen as very long

parts.note: 1 mm, one millimetre, written as I MM

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters are put in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: A tiny distance is mistakenly perceived as enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of '1 mm' is read as the letter I. 'wrongly' rearranges SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge or vast, extending a great way.

clue.text: Baby's hugged close after dark

indicators.note: hugged means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a tot is a baby or small child
nigh means near, close

explanation.surface: An infant is cuddled close once night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening, the coming night.

clue.text: Old Greek unlikely to take to the piano?

definitions.meaning: a herald in the Iliad famous for his loud voice

definitions.text: unlikely to take to the piano?
definitions.meaning: piano is the musical direction for quietly, which a loud-voiced person would avoid

explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric herald had a voice as loud as fifty men, so he would never play quietly.

clue.text: Tremble with fear as second half of Northern town disappears

indicators.note: half of points to one half of the town's twelve-letter name being kept
disappears means the other, second half of the name goes away

parts.note: Huddersfield is a town in West Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: People tremble as part of a northern town vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Huddersfield is a town in West Yorkshire, northern England; only its first six letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver or quake from fright.

clue.text: Martial art hurt enlisted man before exercise is all over

indicators.note: all over means turned right over, so the whole run is read backwards
before means the first pieces come ahead of the next

parts.note: to mar is to hurt or spoil
GI is an American enlisted soldier
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A soldier is injured just before training ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Martial was a Roman poet famed for witty short verses; 'is all over' turns MARGIPE right round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet Martial's skill was the short witty poem.

clue.text: Rest of herb just about dies off

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the herb goes round the other letters

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: The rest of a herb nearly dies off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning remainder; 'off' rearranges the letters of 'dies', and 'just about' puts the herb round them.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the main part is gone, the remainder.

clue.text: Bringing powder for guns was mischievous activity

definitions.meaning: boys called powder monkeys carried gunpowder to warship guns, so this was their job

explanation.definitionFit: Ship's powder monkeys did the gunpowder fetching; the phrase also means tomfoolery.

clue.text: Little room for joiner

definitions.meaning: a small cosy room, especially a small bar parlour in a pub
a carpenter wants pieces to fit closely together

explanation.definitionFit: A small cosy pub room, and a tight fit, which a carpenter aims for.

clue.text: Instruction to break dull march

indicators.note: to break into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bland means dull
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: An order is given to interrupt a boring parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like a verb but is the noun for a frontier region.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is an old word for a frontier district between two countries.

clue.text: Insect that's chewed in India, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken and sounds like the answer

parts.note: betel is the leaf and nut chewed in South Asia

explanation.surface: An insect is eaten in India, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-winged bug is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Unrepeatable performance of show

parts.note: suggests something shocking, but means a show's opening night, which by its nature cannot happen twice

explanation.definitionFit: A first public performance can only happen once.
